pairs.why: B's locomotive sits square on the rails with connecting rods linking the driving wheels and a tender behind, while A's front is a skewed block whose red wheels hang off the boiler at a different angle from the track.

B's wagon has a hitch tongue and wheels mounted on axles under the bed in one consistent three-quarter view, while A's canvas has a hollow tunnel opening and its near rear wheel is oversized compared with the other wheels.
A's fins, portholes and nozzle all follow the tilted round body and the nozzle ring reads as a proper ellipse, while B's portholes face the viewer flat on a body seen at an angle.
A's folding frame works like the real card's chair, with straight back posts, crossed legs and a floor bar, while B's crossed legs and armrest posts tangle at the pivots in a way that would not fold.
B's lifebuoy hangs on a post and its rope wraps a bollard, all on pilings going into the water, while A shows a reflection of the lifebuoy in open water far from the pier where it actually hangs.
A's labeled keys sit in rows that follow the tilted face, like the real calculator, while B's blank keys form an even grid that doesn't foreshorten with the body.
A's lasso is a believable coil with the loop tied off by a knot, while B's large loop joins the coil at a loose sleeve and its tail end dangles with nothing holding it.

B's cat sits squarely on the floor with its body, head and tail seen from one viewpoint, while A's head is turned in profile on a body seen from the front and its tail curls flat against the floor at odds with the planks' perspective.
